questions.q: What do you need to do before AUTOTUNE?
options: Nothing — it does everything by itself
Filters and a base roll/pitch tune
Remove the props and run it on the bench
questions.explain: Filters/notch and a manual or QuikTune roll-pitch: AUTOTUNE starts from the current values and aborts on noise.
The best mode: it tracks each motor.

questions.q: How do you find the noise frequency for a throttle-based notch?
options: Calculate it from the motor KV and battery voltage
A raw IMU spectrum at hover
Derive it from the prop size
questions.explain: Batch sampling/raw IMU before the filters: INS_LOG_BAT_MASK = 1, OPT = 0, then the spectrum at hover.

questions.q: When are the AUTOTUNE results saved?
options: Right after each axis finishes in flight

questions.q: What do you do if the motors get hot after AUTOTUNE?
options: Lower I and raise P on all axes
questions.explain: High D on a noisy gyro: filters/notch, AUTOTUNE_MIN_D, repeat.

questions.q: Why do you enable the batch sampler before the notch?
options: To see the gyro spectrum before and after the filters
To write the parameters to a file
questions.explain: Batch sampling gives you the raw spectrum: you use it to choose the notch frequency and to verify the result.
